content: {"like": ["Color saturation has been toned down to a less jarring degree and the colors do not look bad this time around.", "Ghosting issues present in the first three releases are gone.", "The new cast is enjoyable and provides a consistent dub for the entire series.", "The set has merits despite its flaws, and the reviewer appreciates the improved image compared to earlier releases."], "dislike": ["Image detail is jagged and suffers from the remastering process.", "Digital imperfections were introduced when attempting to remove film/video tape grain.", "The remastering process took away from image detail and created new digital imperfections.", "The lack of film masters (only videotape masters were used) results in a lower quality image.", "Uncalibrated TVs produce oversaturated colors, sharpness, and a soap‑opera effect that makes the content look poor.", "Watching on a 4K TV highlights the faults of Viz's remastering process and distracts from enjoyment.", "Tape marks are visible during scene transitions on the original Sailor Moon S DVDs.", "Overall, the image is not perfect and does not look as good as other programs like Ranma 1/2 or Dragon Ball Z." ]}
